Record allocated descriptor immediately after open, owning process PID, optional expected device/inode, attempt state, status and observation. Constructor cleanup reuses close(), which reuses the unchanged shared close_owned helper, exactly once.
changes.observation: Under the existing RLock, post-attempt fstat EBADF records released_observed/descriptor_absent. Valid descriptors, unknown identity, changed identity and diagnostic failure remain unresolved; matching device/inode is not authority to retry. The closed flag only denies further journal use. Repeated close performs no syscall and does not change unresolved status.

Secondary cleanup interrupts and diagnostic failures do not mask the primary exception, errno or origin frame. No returned partial journal object or hidden traceback retention is needed.

Constructor compound faults preserve primary identity, errno and reached origin traceback frame while retaining public ownership evidence after exception catch.

First owned-file fstat failure before identity assignment still retains the allocated descriptor and process ownership; successful diagnostic reports identity_unknown, diagnostic SystemExit reports diagnostic_failed, both unresolved and actually locked.

Descriptor reused for another inode or the exact same journal inode is never reclosed; both remain unresolved. Same-inode equality cannot prove continuous fd identity.

A separate process remains locked until normal worker exit; kernel process teardown then permits reopening. No harness/manual descriptor close is counted as that recovery.

residual_boundaries: Unresolved ownership is an explicit supported handoff, not physical release. Retain PublicationJournal.cleanup_ownership or original_exception.journal_cleanup_ownership as pending process ownership until separately authorized controlled teardown of that owning process. No automatic os._exit, process kill, manager stub or unsafe fd retry was added.

The old unconditional constructor oracle requiring zero live descriptors after every cleanup failure needs migration to the documented unresolved-handoff boundary. It was not rerun/edited and is not claimed to pass; the original failed report is preserved.

EBADF, fd numbers and device/inode observations do not grant close authority or prove continuous fd identity/lock release. Diagnostic failures are unresolved even when independent evidence observes actual release.

Advisory cooperative locks do not establish hostile same-UID/privileged exclusion, workspace construction identity, multifile atomicity, recovery or world admission. Schema/model/world contracts remain unchanged.
